# Flash Memory Protection Module Specification

## Overview

This module performs flash memory access protection. It evaluates incoming flash requests against software-programmable protection regions and per-bank erase permissions. It decides whether a request is permitted to proceed to the flash memory. If permitted, the requested operation is forwarded. A permission failure suppresses forwarding. Both permission failures and address errors produce an error completion.

## Request Model

Each request includes:

- A flash page address.
- A partition indicator, selecting either the data partition or the information partition.
- A bank selection.
- An operation type: read, program, page erase, or bank erase.
- An overflow indicator that identifies addresses outside the implemented flash address space.

A request shall assert exactly one operation type at a time.

## Configuration

The module is configured with a set of memory protection regions and a set of bank erase permissions.

### Region Configuration

Each region provides:

- A base page address.
- A region size, with the end address exclusive. A zero-size region covers no addresses.
- A partition select, matching either the data partition or the information partition.
- An enable bit.
- Read permission.
- Program permission.
- Page erase permission.

Regions may overlap. When multiple enabled regions match the same request, the region with the lowest index has priority. The selected region is the lowest-index matching region. Only the selected region’s permissions are considered; a lower-priority region cannot grant permission if the selected region denies it.

### Bank Erase Configuration

Bank erase permissions are configured separately per bank. These permissions apply only to bank erase operations and are independent of region permissions.

## Access Evaluation

### Read, Program, and Page Erase

A read, program, or page erase request is allowed only if all of the following conditions are true:

- The overflow indicator is not asserted.
- The request address falls within the range of an enabled region.
- The request partition matches the region’s partition.
- The lowest-index matching region has the permission enabled for the requested operation type.
- If the request targets the information partition, the page address is within the valid information page range.

If no enabled region matches, or if the selected region does not permit the operation, the request is denied.

### Bank Erase

A bank erase request is allowed only if all of the following conditions are true:

- The overflow indicator is not asserted.
- The request targets the data partition.
- The targeted bank has bank erase permission enabled.
- The bank erase request targets exactly one bank.

Bank erase to the information partition is never allowed.

Bank erase does not depend on memory protection region permissions.

## Denial Conditions

A request shall be denied if any of the following apply:

- The overflow indicator is asserted.
- The request is a read, program, or page erase, and no selected region permits the operation.
- The request is a read, program, or page erase to an invalid information page address.
- The request is a bank erase and the target partition is the information partition.
- The request is a bank erase and the targeted bank does not have bank erase permission enabled.

## Output Behavior

### Permitted Requests

When a request is permitted, the module forwards the requested operation to the flash memory side. The forwarded operation preserves the intended address, bank, partition, and operation type.

Completion for a permitted request is reported when the flash memory side completes the operation. No error is reported for a permitted request.

### Denied Requests

When the requested operation lacks permission, no operation is forwarded to the flash memory side. The module returns an error completion for permission failures and address errors.

The error completion shall include:

- An error indication.
- The address of the denied request.
- The bank of the denied request.

A denied request shall produce exactly one error completion in response to the denied request.
